readerFields.title: Earth System Sciences

audience.programmeDescription: Earth System Sciences at Wageningen studies how soil, water, the atmosphere and the biosphere interact. English-taught scientific study combines physics, chemistry, mathematics, modelling and extensive practical work.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme combines Earth processes, climate, soils, water and environmental evidence. The second gives greater weight to geospatial and computational methods; the third to ecological mechanisms, land use and resilience. WUR adds its deeper atmospheric, hydrological and sedimentological sequence, coordinated field courses and required individual thesis.

componentNotes.y1-math-choice: This example uses Mathematics Applied: Introduction for students with VWO Mathematics A. Students with Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead; the choice follows prior preparation and study advice.
componentNotes.y1-intro: The programme also includes non-credit personal development across three years. General, laboratory and fieldwork safety training applies to the relevant practical activities; these requirements are not extra EC.
componentNotes.y3-hydrogeology: One of three selected advanced options. This course combines aquifer systems, groundwater modelling and field investigation. It assumes earlier water-analysis and water-quantity/quality study and requires fieldwork safety.
componentNotes.y3-python: One of three selected advanced options. This course develops Python programming for scientific data work; it assumes elementary computer skills.
componentNotes.y3-sedimentary: One of three selected advanced options. This course studies sedimentary successions and lowland stratigraphy through field and laboratory methods. It builds on the common geology course and requires laboratory and fieldwork safety.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: The required 12 EC thesis is individual Earth-system research. Entry requires at least 102 EC of compulsory and restricted courses, all 60 first-year EC, and the first two years of personal-development assignments or an agreed subset. Supervisors may specify prior-course knowledge for a topic. UCR’s optional 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC.
componentNotes.y3-electives: The illustrated pathway preserves 30 EC for a minor and/or individually chosen electives. Optional data-science courses or a named minor are not made compulsory.
componentNotes.y1-atmosphere: WUR studies atmospheric thermodynamics, radiation, cloud physics, chemistry and dynamics quantitatively. UCR’s Climate Change course addresses greenhouse forcing, feedbacks and impacts, without the same dedicated atmospheric-physics sequence.
componentNotes.y2-interactions: WUR explicitly models soil–vegetation–atmosphere exchanges, evapotranspiration, radiation and transport. General ecological energy and matter cycles at UCR do not reproduce that coupled physical sequence.

concepts: Study geological, soil, water and climate processes through field and laboratory evidence, geochemical and numerical models, ecological relationships and environmental responses. Energy systems and governance connect that scientific understanding to practical sustainability questions.

Investigate environmental change through GIS and remote sensing, programming, statistics, numerical methods and predictive models. Ground computational work in Earth-system, climate, soil and water mechanisms, while examining adaptation and governance.

Study how soil and water processes interact with biodiversity, ecosystems and land use. Combine geoscience and environmental chemistry with ecological measurement, conservation, farming, nature-based water management and environmental justice.

notes.text: WUR prescribes a deeper sequence in atmospheric physics and meteorology, hydrology, general chemistry, lowland sedimentology and coordinated field measurement, followed by an individual 12 EC thesis. The UCR programmes combine substantial Earth science, geochemistry, soils, water, ecology and geospatial or quantitative inquiry. They do not reproduce that full specialist sequence. UCR’s optional 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC.

selectedCourseDescriptions.name: Governance of Sustainability
selectedCourseDescriptions.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
